summary: A first-person travelogue-style essay reflecting on trickster tales across cultures, drawing on dated conversations from September 2023 to March 2026 in places like New Orleans, Durban, Japan, Arizona, Los Angeles, Berlin and Cadiz. Each encounter shows a different facet of the trickster: survival through wit, storyteller and teacher, moral ambiguity, agent of change, modern inspiration, catalyst for debate, and communal celebration. The author concludes that tricksters upset the ordinary and impart wisdom in unconventional ways.
one_line: Personal essay exploring trickster figures from Compère Lapin to Loki through conversations in several countries, showing their roles as teachers, agents of change and mirrors of society.
key_facts: On September 3, 2023, at a dinner party in New Orleans, Lorraine Dubois told the tale of Compère Lapin (Brother Rabbit), a Creole trickster similar to the Br'er Rabbit of the Southern United States.
Lorraine Dubois said Compère Lapin "represents the spirit of survival and the notion that wit can triumph over brute strength."
On May 12, 2024, in South Africa, storyteller Stanley Mkhize of Durban told tales of Anansi, the spider of West African and Caribbean folklore, whom he called "the keeper of all stories."
On November 16, 2024, in Japan, Professor Keiko Tanaka of Tokyo University explained that kitsune (fox) and tanuki (raccoon dog) are shapeshifters who are "neither good nor evil."
Professor Keiko Tanaka said kitsune and tanuki tales prompt reflection on deceit and teach that every action carries consequences.

On February 21, 2025, Hopi elder Frank Sun Bear in Arizona described Kokopelli, the humpbacked flute player, as "a spirit of change, fertility, and transition," while watching the sunset over the red rocks of Sedona.

On September 7, 2025, Los Angeles screenwriter Eva Sanchez, a Mexican-American, said she drew on the trickster god Huehuecoyotl for her animated film's protagonist, a clever coyote with a penchant for trouble.

On December 9, 2025, a panel discussion in Berlin debated whether Loki, the Norse god of mischief, is a necessary chaotic force that challenges the status quo or a problematic character whose actions excuse duplicity.
On March 3, 2026, the Carnival in Cadiz, Spain, featured parades and satirical performances embodying trickster spirit.
José García, a masked Carnival participant in Cadiz embodying the 'Picaro' archetype from Spanish literature, said "We all have a little 'Picaro' in us."
The author argues trickster tales are not mere relics of the past but continue to influence modern storytelling and pop culture.
The essay concludes that tricksters upset the ordinary, challenge perceptions and impart wisdom in unconventional ways, acting as teachers without podiums.
